# Broker direct-caller allow-list — IMP-056 SCOPE-6
#
# mutable-dispatch-caller-coverage-lint.sh fails any file (other than
# reference-broker.sh itself and mutable-dispatch-gateway.sh) that invokes
# reference-broker.sh's `dispatch` verb directly, since every production
# dispatch must route through the gateway's adapter-resolve + shared-snapshot
# + mint/verify sequence. A file listed here is a deliberate exception: it
# tests the broker itself in isolation and is not a production call site.
#
# Each entry MUST be preceded by a comment line giving the reason. The lint
# fails when an entry has no reason, and when a listed file no longer exists
# (so this file cannot rot).
#
# Format: one repo-relative path per line. Blank lines and `#` comments
# ignored.

# Adversarial/unit-level tests of reference-broker.sh in isolation (snapshot
# creation, launch-state ledger transitions, permit consumption, the
# mutableDispatchAudit block) — calling the broker directly is the point of
# this suite, and it never represents a production dispatch path.
bubbles/scripts/measured-budget-runtime-v2-selftest.py

# This lint's own selftest writes red-fixture heredocs (evil-direct.sh,
# evil-indirect.sh, broker-adversarial-selftest.sh) into throwaway mktemp
# trees to prove the lint catches a bypass. Those fixture bytes live inside
# THIS file's own source text, so a scan of the real repository sees the same
# literal bypass-shaped lines this lint is supposed to detect. Same precedent
# as agnosticity-allowlist.txt exempting agnosticity-lint-selftest.sh.
bubbles/scripts/mutable-dispatch-caller-coverage-lint-selftest.sh
